variants.title: Reason about a snapshot
variants.context: Transaction isolation determines which concurrent changes a transaction can observe.
variants.prompt: Two SELECT statements run under Read Committed, and another transaction commits between them. Can the second SELECT observe newer data?
options: Yes, the statements can see different committed snapshots.
No, Read Committed fixes a transaction-wide snapshot.
No, SELECT prevents every other transaction from committing.

variants.explanation: Read Committed takes a new snapshot for each statement.

variants.title: Measure work per useful row
variants.context: Query efficiency compares database work with the rows the application actually needs. This exercise counts examined rows per returned row.
variants.prompt: A plan examines 10000 rows and returns 10. On average, how many examined rows is that per returned row?
variants.hint: Divide examined rows by returned rows.
variants.explanation: 10000 / 10 = 1000. This ratio is a clue to investigate, not proof that one specific index is best.

variants.title: Put a rule at the data boundary

variants.prompt: Every stored short code must be unique. What should enforce it?
